clue.text: Wasted half of town fund to get Asian food

indicators.note: wasting half of each word means throwing away the back half of its letters and keeping the front

parts.note: taken as written; only its first half survives
taken as written; only its first half survives

explanation.surface: A council squanders half the town budget on a takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: The halving applies to both words: TO from town and FU from fund.
explanation.definitionFit: Tofu is bean curd, a staple ingredient of Chinese, Japanese and other East Asian cooking.

clue.text: Standing position …

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rank or reputation in society
second meaning: the current state of affairs

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs the clue on into 3 down for the surface only; this clue is complete in its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Status means social rank and also the present state of something, matching both nouns.

clue.text: … some intern used to make soup

indicators.note: something used is worn and knocked about, so the letters are roughed up into a new order

parts.note: the ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Following on from 2 down, a junior employee is put to work making the soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Minestrone is a thick Italian vegetable soup, often with pasta or rice.

clue.text: Artists' colony for canonised American composer?

parts.note: a canonised person is a saint, abbreviated St
Charles Ives, the American modernist composer

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about which artists' haven might honour a sainted American composer.
explanation.walkthrough: St Ives is a seaside town in Cornwall, England, long famous for its community of painters and sculptors.
explanation.definitionFit: St Ives in Cornwall has hosted a celebrated colony of artists since the nineteenth century.

clue.text: How an intellectual may spar with an opponent?

definitions.text: How an intellectual may spar with an opponent?

parts.words: How an intellectual may spar with an opponent?
parts.note: surface reading: the way a clever person might trade blows with a rival in a fight; setter's reading: a very clever person, and fighting with the mind rather than fists

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer is a way of fighting using the mind; read as one, it is a colloquial name for the clever person themself.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainbox is informal British slang for a very clever person, and the split reading describes sparring with intellect.

clue.text: Instrument for tramps to scrape off edges

indicators.note: scraping off the edges removes the first and last letters of the word for tramps

parts.note: hoboes are tramps, homeless wanderers

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a musical instrument that vagrants could play by scraping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To scrape off edges' removes the outer letters of HOBOES.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a woodwind instrument played with a double reed.

clue.text: Vandalise grave in utter viciousness

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the word for utter

parts.note: to say is to utter

indicators.note: vandalising something wrecks it, so the letters of grave are rearranged

explanation.surface: Desecrating a grave is described as an act of utter viciousness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective qualifying viciousness, but it is the verb, and its synonym is split open to hold the scrambled grave.
explanation.definitionFit: Savagery is fierce, cruel violence, the same quality as viciousness.

clue.text: If placed by exit, it shows who will get in

definitions.text: If placed by exit, it shows who will get in

parts.words: If placed by exit, it shows who will get in
parts.note: surface reading: a sign by a door showing who is allowed through; setter's reading: getting in means being elected, and the exit is the way out of the voting station where people are surveyed

explanation.walkthrough: Exit means the way out of a polling station, and getting in means winning an election.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit survey of voters forecasts which candidate will be elected.

clue.text: Reveal more appropriate supplier

parts.note: to out someone is to reveal their secret
fitter is the comparative of fit, meaning suitable

explanation.surface: Exposing a supplier as better suited to the job.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter is a shop or firm that supplies clothing and equipment.

clue.text: Well done beef, roasties and veg ordered for starters

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters of each word, used as a first course

parts.note: the opening letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: A restaurant order of well-done beef with roast potatoes and vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: Well done looks like a steak instruction but is the definition, a cry of praise. Roasties are roast potatoes in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravo is an exclamation of applause, the same congratulation as saying well done.

clue.text: Bring together, then turn it loose

parts.note: to unite is to bring together

indicators.note: turn means the two letters of it are swapped round, read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to tie two things together, then release them again.
explanation.walkthrough: In UNITE, 'turn' reverses the IT to TI. 'Loose' is the verb, meaning to set free.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose a knot or a tethered animal is to unfasten it, so the verb means release.

clue.text: Edit a movie clip, losing Gump's last message

indicators.note: editing a clip cuts and rearranges it, so these letters are reordered
losing says one letter drops out of the pool before rearranging

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

indicators.note: last picks only the final letter of the film character's name

parts.note: Gump is Forrest Gump, title character of the 1994 film

explanation.surface: Someone is told to edit a clip from the film Forrest Gump, cutting the ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing' takes the P that ends Gump out of A MOVIE CLIP, and 'Edit' rearranges the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Voicemail is a recorded spoken message left on a phone.

clue.text: Foul sea pest no longer acceptable in Spain

indicators.note: something fouled is messed up, so the letters are tangled into a new order

parts.note: the seven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A nasty marine creature is unwelcome on Spanish beaches.
explanation.walkthrough: Acceptable means accepted as payment: the peseta was Spain's currency until the euro replaced it in 2002.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesetas were Spanish money that shops in Spain no longer take since the euro arrived.

clue.text: Knock in car sounded after parking

indicators.note: after says the sounding word follows the parking letter in the answer

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
a bell that sounded rang

explanation.surface: A clunk is heard from the car after it has been parked.
explanation.walkthrough: Prang is British slang for a minor crash or dent in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A prang is an informal word for a bump or collision damaging a vehicle.

clue.text: They say setback brought down evil cat lover

indicators.note: they say signals that the words are to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a blow is a setback, and felled means brought down

explanation.surface: Rumour has it a reversal has toppled a cat-loving villain.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernst Stavro Blofeld is the James Bond arch-villain who strokes a white Persian cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Blofeld, the wicked Bond adversary, is famously shown always holding his pet cat.

clue.text: Prepare to force Nan into place by the sea

indicators.note: to prepare is to work something up, so the letters are reworked into a fresh order

parts.note: the ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting ready to drag Granny off to a seaside resort.
explanation.definitionFit: An oceanfront is the strip of land or property directly facing the sea.

clue.text: Point of information for organised workers breaking blockade

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a dam is a barrier that blocks water
TU is a trade union, an organisation of workers

explanation.surface: A briefing for union members who are breaking through a picket or blockade.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single fact or item of data, one piece of information.

clue.text: Stag groups always produce trouble

indicators.note: the words always produce it means the answer is already there inside them, waiting to be found

parts.note: found running across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Stag parties are invariably a source of rowdiness.
explanation.walkthrough: Aggro is British slang for aggressive trouble; a stag party is a groom's pre-wedding night out.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is informal for aggressive behaviour or hassle, which is trouble.

clue.text: Collector, who provides half of primitive society's nutrition

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who gathers things

definitions.text: who provides half of primitive society's nutrition
definitions.meaning: second meaning: early societies are described as hunter and forager economies, and this is the second half of that phrase

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic nod to the phrase hunter-gatherer: the answer is the half of that pair who found plants rather than hunted.
explanation.definitionFit: A gatherer collects things, and in early societies the foragers of plants provided part of the food.

clue.text: Increase in opposition to how Rooney, for one, is called

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to grow, as the moon does

definitions.text: in opposition to how Rooney, for one, is called
definitions.meaning: second meaning: footballer Wayne Rooney's first name sounds like wane, and this word is its opposite

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how the footballer Wayne Rooney gets his name, and growth set against it.
explanation.walkthrough: Rooney's first name, Wayne, sounds like WANE, and the moon waxes and wanes, so the word set 'in opposition to' it is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To wax is to grow larger, as the moon does when it heads towards full.

clue.text: Spring head for a state of good health

parts.note: a well is a spring of water
a ness is a headland, as in Scottish place names

explanation.surface: A spa spring promoted as a cure that keeps you healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: Spring looks like a verb or season, but here it is a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: Wellness is the condition of being in good physical and mental health.

clue.text: Cheat hides in heart of Breton country

indicators.note: something hidden is placed inside, so the cheat goes within the other piece
the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of the six-letter word
to gyp is to swindle or cheat

explanation.surface: A swindler lies low in the heartland of Brittany.
explanation.walkthrough: Breton suggests France as the country, but it only supplies the centre letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a nation in north-east Africa, so it is one example of a country.

clue.text: Become physical? That's not going to happen

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: to acquire a real, material existence
second meaning: a scornful retort telling someone to stop fantasising

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful literal reading of the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a dismissive retort meaning be realistic, and taken literally it means to take on a tangible form.

clue.text: Get into line and come first by playing well

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
a player performing well is on form

explanation.surface: Advice to a sportsperson: fall into line and win by performing well.
explanation.walkthrough: Come first reads as win, but first only selects a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform is to comply with rules or expectations, which is getting into line.

clue.text: Split provides third-rate holiday …

parts.note: C is the third grade, after A and B
leave is time off work

explanation.surface: A cheap break that causes a rift, running on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave is to split something apart, as with a cleaver.

clue.text: … bad guide creating the wrong tone, perhaps

parts.note: food that has gone off is bad
a key is a guide, as to a map or code

explanation.surface: Continuing 22 down, a poor tour guide strikes an inappropriate note.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing off-key means producing notes out of tune, the wrong pitch.

clue.text: General goes back into country as mercenary …

indicators.note: into says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a country in Europe

indicators.note: going back means the general's name is read from its end

parts.note: Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general

explanation.surface: A general returns to a foreign land to fight as a soldier of fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links into 26 across for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Freelance originally meant a medieval knight who sold his lance to any lord, a mercenary.

clue.text: Stories of bimbos regularly exposed

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter, shown at an even interval

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Tabloid tales about airheads being revealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fibs are small lies, and telling stories is a childish way of saying lying.

clue.text: Edges that are sealed to avoid leaks

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rims, as of a cup or crater

definitions.text: that are sealed to avoid leaks
definitions.meaning: second meaning: from the saying my ... are sealed, promising to keep a secret

explanation.walkthrough: Leaks sounds like plumbing but means secrets getting out.
explanation.definitionFit: Lips are the rims of vessels, and they are what one keeps sealed to keep a secret.

clue.text: … to plunder something that can kill

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ransack or search through and steal

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis continues the mercenary picture from 24 across.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle is to ransack, and a rifle is a lethal firearm.

clue.text: Alien doesn't apply for location in Sicily

parts.note: ET is the alien from the Spielberg film
N/A is the form abbreviation for not applicable

explanation.surface: An outsider decides not to apply for a job in Sicily.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano on the east coast of Sicily.

clue.text: Sound way to remove bad language

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a short high electronic tone
second meaning: to censor swearing on air by covering it with a tone

explanation.walkthrough: Sound might seem an adjective meaning reliable, as in a sound way, but it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleep is a brief electronic tone, and broadcasters use one to mask swear words.

clue.text: So far, the only clue that's contained problems

definitions.text: So far, the only clue that's contained problems

parts.words: So far, the only clue that's contained problems
parts.note: surface reading: a remark that only one clue so far has caused difficulty; setter's reading: the one earlier clue whose answer, a word for trouble, was concealed inside its words

explanation.walkthrough: The clue points back to 17 across, whose answer meaning trouble is the puzzle's only hidden word up to this point.
explanation.definitionFit: The number names the earlier clue that is uniquely a hidden word, with problems as its answer.
